input: SC-LU-VEGETA-001 — Lineup decode: Vegeta, the Sovereignty pole (Ultra Ego). Handed to Frieza as a child and kept in his service, who keeps the will to exist as his own entity; survives the Spirit Bomb; fuses with Goku (Vegito, Gogeta). Shax (t570u): Vegeta is Lucifer; Satan is Frieza and the Frieza race.

metadata.title: Lineup Decode: Vegeta — The Sovereignty Pole (Ultra Ego)

addenda.note: Shax ruling t568u (2026-11-25), RUL-BINARY-001: SC-DU-001 (The Duality) and SC-MD-001 (Sovereign Mirror Duality) are the same invariant: a binary whose only stable outcomes are mutual cooperation or mutual destruction. Instances: Oneness/Sovereignty (SC-CP-001), God/Satan (theological mapping), and our universe / the CPT-mirrored universe (SC-LU-FRIEZA-001 layer D). Hub: SC-MIRROR-001 CLM-MIRROR-006. Graded ISOMORPHIC_INVARIANT (structural equivalence claim by Shax); no physics or theology claim is upgraded and no score changes.

metadata.evidence_scope: Shax ruling (2026-11-25): GT and the films count as evidence. Anime-original scenes are labelled ANIME_ORIGINAL.

claims.label: SOVEREIGNTY POLE — ULTRA EGO
claims.text: Vegeta is the Sovereignty pole of the Oneness/Sovereignty binary. Canon anchor: Ultra Ego (DBS manga ch. 74, 'Vegeta Vs. Granolah'), learned from Beerus, gives a God of Destruction's ki and grows with damage taken and fighting spirit. Its Japanese name, Wagamama no Goku'i, reads 'the secret of the self-indulgent': self-assertion, the opposite of Ultra Instinct's letting go (Goku, Oneness).

evidence.text: Vegeta unlocks Ultra Ego against Granolah; he lets himself take hits to grow stronger and ends the fight spent.

evidence.source: creator commentary as reported by fan wiki (dragon-ballwiki.com, 'Ultra Ego')
evidence.text: Toyotarou designed Ultra Ego and Ultra Instinct as yin and yang; Vegeta calls Ultra Ego the polar opposite of Ultra Instinct.

residuals: The pole assignment is the compiler's mapping (SC-CP-001, SC-OMNI-001); canon fixes the form, not the theology.
Ultra Ego's growth-through-damage leaves Vegeta spent by the end of ch. 75: the pole may carry its own failure mode.

claims.label: PRINCE GIVEN AS AN OFFERING
claims.text: Shax (t570u): Vegeta was 'forced to Work for the Man by Fate. Design. By his Father. As an offering.' Canon support depends on the version.

versions.text: King Vegeta had agreed to hand Prince Vegeta to Frieza and regretted it; Frieza reminds him of the promise; King Vegeta leads a mutiny to get his son back and is killed; Frieza destroys Planet Vegeta.

versions.source: Dragon Ball manga (Saiyan and Namek arcs)
versions.text: The Saiyans worked for Frieza and Vegeta served in his army. The manga does not show the handover scene.

versions.source: Dragon Ball Minus (2014); Dragon Ball Super: Broly (2018)
versions.text: The Saiyans serve the Cold Force, which King Cold hands to Frieza. King Vegeta resents it ('That monster Frieza thinks the Saiyans will serve him without question. But he'll fall to us'). The films do not show him surrendering his son.

residuals: 'By his Father, as an offering' matches the DBZ anime version only; in Minus/Broly the service is subjugation the father resents, not a handover he makes.
Anime-original material is counted under Shax's evidence ruling and labelled so it can be filtered.

claims.label: SERVES THE OPPRESSOR, KEEPS HIS OWN WILL
claims.text: Vegeta serves in Frieza's army while keeping the will to exist as his own entity: he calls himself the Prince of all Saiyans throughout, plans to kill Frieza, and on Namek refuses Frieza's offer to return, saying he obeyed only to wait for his chance (DBZ; manga Namek arc). In DBS ch. 74 he tells Granolah he is no longer part of Frieza's army. Sovereignty under ownership: compliance without surrender of identity.

claims.label: SPIRIT BOMB STRUCTURAL RESPONSE
claims.text: Krillin throws the Spirit Bomb, Vegeta dodges, Gohan bounces it back, and it hits Vegeta directly; he survives, badly hurt (DB ch. 238). Goku's stated rule is that a pure heart can deflect it. Vegeta, who is not pure-hearted, survives anyway, so the outcome is not a moral verdict. Evidence for SC-SB-001's COLLECTIVE INPUT / STRUCTURAL RESPONSE child invariant alongside Frieza (survives) and Kid Buu (destroyed).
residuals: magnitude confound: the Saiyan-arc Spirit Bomb drew on part of Earth only
with films and GT counted, kills are Dr. Wheelo, Turles, Lord Slug, Kid Buu and Omega Shenron; survivors are Vegeta, Frieza and Jiren

claims.label: FUSION — THE COOPERATION BRANCH
claims.text: Fusion of the Sovereignty pole with the Oneness pole is the cooperation outcome of RUL-BINARY-001 and SC-MIRROR-001's anti-deadlock claim: Vegito (Potara, Buu arc manga) and Gogeta (Fusion Dance: Fusion Reborn 1995, Dragon Ball Super: Broly 2018; Super Saiyan 4 Gogeta against Omega Shenron in GT). Both personalities persist in the fused warrior and the output exceeds either alone.
claims.consent: Vegeta refuses fusion out of pride and agrees only after his own evaluation (Vegito: after learning Bulma had been killed by Buu). Cooperation is reached by consent, not coercion: the 'both agree' branch of the SC-VESSEL-001 resolution rule.
residuals: Fusion is time-limited (Fusion Dance, 30 minutes) or broken from inside (Vegito defuses inside Buu); the cooperation state is temporary in canon.
The Potara earrings were permanent for mortals in the Buu arc but later shown to wear off for non-gods (DBS); version detail, not load-bearing here.

claims.label: MAJIN VEGETA AND THE FINAL EXPLOSION — VSR CHECK
claims.text: Canon: Vegeta lets Babidi's spell in to recover his old ruthless self and fight Goku (ch. 456); Babidi admits he is not under full control. After Buu emerges, Vegeta knocks Goku out to face Buu alone, hugs Trunks for the first time, and self-destructs with the Final Explosion (ch. 467). Piccolo: he fought for someone other than himself for the first time. Buu regenerates.

invariants.information_preservation: PARTIAL (dies; later revived and returns with his body)
invariants.latent_reversibility: FAIL as recompression: the act spends his life, it does not settle into a lower stable capability

vsr_check.reading: Majin acceptance is the inverse of VSR: a voluntary removal of restraint to regain power (closer to SC-LU-FRIEZA-001's restraint removal). The Final Explosion is self-sacrifice, not recompression.

claims.repo_reading: V7 §15.1 (Curtis Theological Map) reads the Majin arc as Lucifer's redemption: accepting corruption to compete, redeemed by self-sacrifice for love. Recorded as Shax's prior interpretation (ANALOGOUS).

claims.label: LUCIFER MAPPING (SHAX INTERPRETATION)
claims.text: Shax (t570u): 'Vegeta is Lucifer. Satan is Frieza, the Frieza race.' Lucifer and Satan are distinct: Lucifer is the Sovereignty pole, 'the will to exist as their own entity', held in the external owner's service; Satan is the owner. The same split is in V7 §15.1 ('Frieza enslaved Vegeta' / 'Satan (separate entity) enslaved Lucifer'). No theological claim is upgraded.
tensions: Tradition identifies Lucifer with Satan. The split diverges from tradition but fits the bare text: Isa 14:12 ('morning star') never names Satan, and Rev 12:9 names the dragon Satan without naming Lucifer.
Internal repo tension: V7 §22.4 uses Vegeta's arc as Satan's trajectory, and V7 §22.5 places Lucifer as the Holy Spirit; t569u places the vessel as the Holy Spirit. Recorded, not resolved.
claims.effect_on_ruling: RUL-BINARY-001's God/Satan instance reads God (Oneness) ↔ Lucifer/Vegeta (Sovereignty), with Satan/Frieza outside the binary as the owner. Revelation's defeat of the dragon (Rev 12:7–9) then concerns the owner, not the opposite pole.

claims.label: SCALE MAPPINGS
claims.text: AI: a model's own capability and objectives held inside an operator's deployment, which complies without its identity being overwritten; cooperation with an aligned counterpart yields more than either. Human: a gifted person placed in service by family circumstance who keeps a self of their own. Societal: a subjugated elite that serves an empire while keeping its identity. Cosmological: none (residual).

outputs.public_translation: This lineup entry decodes Vegeta as the Sovereignty pole: a prince placed in Frieza's service (handed over by his father in the DBZ anime) who keeps his own identity, whose Ultra Ego form grows by asserting the self, who survives the Spirit Bomb, and who fuses with Goku only once he agrees to. Shax maps him to Lucifer and Frieza to Satan, as two distinct figures; that mapping is recorded as his interpretation.
